tagline: Good evening. This is SIGNAL LOST.

decks.name: Sign-On
decks.world: A cathedral radio warming up in a dark room: cold filaments, then the dial lamp, the band of kilocycle ticks, the needle hunting and locking on 1230, the magic-eye tube closing on a strong signal. Tonight's headline comes off the RSS feed and seeds the script; the theme swells; the ON AIR lamp lights; and the announcer says the only line every episode shares. Midnight bakelite, dial amber, cream paper, magic-eye green, one red lamp.

palette.why: Cream dial glass and script paper.
Magic-eye green for signal; the ON AIR lamp is the one red.
Cue markup in Courier; captions in Bahnschrift.

text_corpus: GOOD EVENING. THIS IS SIGNAL LOST.
moments: Warm up to lock: Scene Launch 1 with every fader low, walk UP one column per bar while raising fader 4 (LIGHT) so the dial lamp comes up with the filaments; the needle locks on column 3.
Good evening: Scene Launch 6 on the downbeat, tap the row-5 TEXT pad so the caption retypes, and leave the ON AIR lamp on its own slow pulse. Do not touch an effect for a phrase.
Act one: UP to column 7, Device knob 2 (TEXTURE) to a third with CRT lit so the act card reads as a title card on a print; drop it to zero on the first line of dialogue.

decks.name: Writers Room
decks.world: The script's birth, node by node: OTR_LedgerScriptWriter takes a premise, characters, a plot and a setting and writes the play; the parser pulls [SFX:] [MUSIC:] [BEAT] [PAUSE] [ACT] out of the text; OTR_LedgerFreezeCascade normalizes it for speech and audits visual coverage; then the ledger locks and the script becomes the source of truth for every later node. Nodes are amber boxes on ruled cream paper, wired; the locked ledger turns magic-eye green.

palette.why: Widget names in Courier, exactly as the node shows them.

moments: Premise to setting: walk UP through columns 1-4 one per phrase; the wires on row 3 wobble on the mids. Keep every effect off so the node boxes read.
Beat: fire Scene Launch 6 exactly on a dropped beat in the music and let the room hold - the SCOPE goes flat on purpose.
Freeze to lock: UP to column 7 with Device knob 6 (ECHO) at a quarter so the cascade's lines stack; UP again to Ledger Locked on the downbeat and tap BANK LOCK (CLEAN).

decks.name: The Cast
decks.world: Who speaks, and in what tongue. OTR_CastLock binds a Kokoro voice to each name for the whole episode; the announcer gets the ring and the ON AIR lamp; eight languages are eight bands under one switch; the voice pool is a field of soft discs with two lit. Dialogue is two sines in exchange, green and amber, never overlapping. Captions are burned in Bahnschrift over a dark bar and mirror the written line. It ends on the credit roll: written, cast, performed, scored, drawn, cut, on one machine.

palette.why: Voice A, the Kokoro sine, green.
Voice B and the phoneme line, amber.
The magic eye for the announcer.

text_corpus: EN ES PT IT FR HI JA ZH
moments: Dialogue: Scene Launch 6 and ride faders 2 and 3 against each other as the voices trade lines; the SCOPE waveform is the master.
Eight languages: Scene Launch 4 with Device knob 3 (SPACE) at a quarter and GRID CLONE lit so the eight bands tile; tap NEGATIVE once per language if the track has eight hits.
Credit roll: UP to column 8 on the last chorus, pull every fader but 5 and 7, and let the credits type over crackle; BLACKOUT on the final beat.

decks.name: The Graph
decks.world: A VJ journey through otr_canonical.json, one node per scene in signal order: ScriptWriter, FreezeCascade, CastLock, Voices, SceneSequencer, Assembler, RenderBatch, MasterAudioMux. Each column is one rounded node on the canvas grid with its real input sockets stacked green down the left edge and its outputs amber down the right, and a wire leaving right toward the next. Until the voices node the wire carries only JSON, a thin line; from there it carries audio and the SCOPE becomes a waveform. The last node is green: the .mp4.

palette.why: Class names and socket names, exact.

moments: The journey: Scene Launch 1 then UP once per bar through all eight nodes; keep Device knob 6 (ECHO) at a quarter so each wire leaves a trace into the next column.
Sockets: on any node, tap the row-3 FIGURE pad and row-4 LIGHT pad alternately on the beat so inputs and outputs blink in turn; the kick swells the dots.
Mux: at column 8 pull faders 1 and 6, leave the green node and the waveform, and tap NEGATIVE for one bar as the file lands.

decks.name: Shivering Gauge
decks.world: The episode itself, drawn as the pack draws everything: a film archivist and an apprentice racing vinegar syndrome through one night in the lab. Storybook-engraving hatching, four developing tanks, two reels, and a gauge whose red needle sits past the line and shivers on the highs. Safelight amber, acetate haze, first light under the door, and the sign-off: this has been SIGNAL LOST. Good night.

palette.why: The gauge needle: red, past the line.

moments: The gauge: Scene Launch 3, hold the row-3 FIGURE pad so the red needle shows only while held; UP to Shivering on the hi-hat run and let the face shake.
Vinegar: column 4, Device knob 3 (SPACE) to a third with WARPSPEED lit so the acetate haze warps the hatching; pull it to zero on the next caption.
Sign-off: UP to column 8 on the last phrase, fade every fader but 2, 3, 5 and 8, let the carrier drop to hiss, then STOP ALL CLIPS.

effect_wishlist.role: Bank A: the freeze cascade stacking, the carrier's afterglow.
Bank A: the bandpass window closing on the full band.
Bank C: engravings and act cards as a print.
Bank C: the sequencer's scene changes.
Bank B: acetate warping in Vinegar.

fft_philosophy: Radio is sound made visible, so the composition's reactivity is the program line and the voices. Mids drive the SCOPE (VU line or waveform) 1:1 and the magic eye's fan; lows drive only size and width - dial lines, node boxes, timeline blocks, filament size - so a kick is pressure on the chassis; highs shiver the band ticks, the hatching and, once, the gauge face. Colour never reacts: amber is work, green is signal and master, cream is paper, red is the ON AIR lamp and the gauge needle and nothing else. Text never moves. [BEAT] and the 48 kHz Master are deliberately still: the picture holds while the sound does the work.
wildcard_rationale: Four decks are the machine: the set signing on, the writers' room, the cast, the filter. The fifth is what the machine made - The Shivering Gauge, the episode the pack's README opens on - drawn the way the pipeline draws its own stills, so the instrument ends by performing its own output.
